newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel tightens grip on Jerusalem before Cairo trip.
newsitem.headline: Israel tightens grip on Jerusalem before Cairo trip.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered police to shut four Palestinian offices in Arab East Jerusalem, flaunting Israel's hold on all the city ahead of a visit to Egypt on Wednesday.

The move, directed against Palestinian Authority activity in Jerusalem, drew quick PLO and Egyptian condemnation at a time of already high tensions over Israel's plan to build new Jewish homes in the city's occupied Arab half.
"I believe that this would be another wrong move," Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told Israel's army radio. "Why should you provoke Arab public opinion?"
"The step has been taken only 24 hours before a visit. I hope there is no connection," Moussa said. Netanyahu was due in Cairo for talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.

Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy dismissed Egypt's consternation. "It is clear -- and I think the Egyptians also know it -- that the Palestinian Authority activities in Jerusalem are against the Oslo agreement," Levy told the radio.
A police spokesman said warnings would be served on Wednesday on the four institutions in East Jerusalem but declined to announce which offices would be ordered shut.

Levy said Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, now on a showcase visit to the United States, had to respect an interim peace deal barring PLO government activity in East Jerusalem, whose status is to be decided in future peace talks.
"We are going to shut down those offices...We are not asking Palestinians to shut them down. We are shutting them down," Netanyahu told U.S. Jewish leaders late on Tuesday.
Netanyahu has come under fire from Jewish settlers and other right-wingers ahead of a planned troop withdrawal from West Bank rural areas slated for Friday.
Israeli media said Netanyahu faced heavy U.S. pressure to increase the scope of the pullback, the first of three due to be completed by mid-1998, to compensate for his moves in Jerusalem.
Israel is to decide the extent of the pullback on Thursday.
Faisal al-Husseini, the top PLO official in Jerusalem, said the threatened closures showed the Israeli government did not care about the peace process.
"Such arbitrary decisions will take the region back to the atmosphere of conflict between the Palestinians and the Israelis, which we had dreamed of ending," he told Voice of Palestine radio.
Last year, the PLO closed two offices in the east of the city after Israel demanded they be shut. The PLO said it closed them to deprive Netanyahu of any excuse to slow peace efforts.

Israel announced the closures only hours after Arafat said in Washington he still regarded Netanyahu as a peace partner despite his plans to build 6,500 Jewish homes at Jabal Abu Ghneim, called Har Homa by Israel.
Netanyahu has said bulldozers will begin to move in two weeks on the pine-covered Jerusalem hill at the centre of an international controversy.
U.S. President Bill Clinton sided with Arafat at a White House meeting on Monday, saying Netanyahu's plan to build the homes in East Jerusalem would fuel "mistrust".
Israel captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed it, a move not recognised internationally, to claim all the city as its capital.
The PLO sees construction at Jabal Abu Ghneim as an attempt to block its demand for East Jerusalem to become capital of a Palestinian state.
